pages.text: Population genetics, run fast. A beneficial mutation fixes with Kimura's probability (1 − e^(−2s))/(1 − e^(−4Ns)). Too small a population and drift beats selection; too high a mutation rate and the genome melts (error catastrophe).
$(thing)Set$(): Population size, Selection coefficient, Mutation rate.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Mutagen drift: µ·(1 ± 20%·d).

$(thing)Limits$(): Drift dominates: selection is blind at this population size; Error catastrophe: mutations outpace selection; The culture is overheating.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Evolution proceeds as fast as adaptations fix.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Genomic mutation rate: U = µL$(br)Fixation probability: P = (1−e^(−2s))/(1−e^(−4Ns))$(br)Adaptation rate: v = 2NU·f_b·P_fix$(br)Selection strength Ns: N·s
